et medlemskab.explanation: "Et medlemskab" means "a membership", being a member of a club, a gym or a group. The ending -skab also makes "et venskab" (a friendship) from "en ven" (a friend).

sentence.da: Et **medlemskab** i klubben koster hundrede kroner om måneden.
sentence.en: A membership in the club costs a hundred kroner a month.

et mellemnavn.explanation: "Et mellemnavn" means "a middle name", a name between the first and last name. It is made of mellem (between) and et navn (a name), and "mellem" also appears in "et mellemmåltid" (a snack between meals).

sentence.da: Marie er mit **mellemnavn**.
sentence.en: Marie is my middle name.

et menneske.explanation: "Et menneske" means "a human being", as opposed to an animal. Its plural "mennesker" is the everyday word for "people", as in "mange mennesker" (many people).

sentence.da: Du er et **menneske**, ikke et dyr.
sentence.en: You are a human being, not an animal.

et menukort.explanation: "Et menukort" means "a menu", the list of dishes and drinks in a restaurant. You can ask a waiter "Må jeg se menukortet?" (May I see the menu?). A set meal with several courses is "en menu" (a set menu).

sentence.da: Vi ser på et **menukort** i restauranten.
sentence.en: We look at a menu in the restaurant.

et mesterskab.explanation: "Et mesterskab" means "a championship", a competition to find the best. Short forms are "DM" (Danish championship), "EM" (European) and "VM" (World). The ending -skab is the same as in "et medlemskab" (a membership).

sentence.da: Vinderen af et **mesterskab** får en guldmedalje.
sentence.en: The winner of a championship gets a gold medal.

et metal.explanation: "Et metal" means "a metal", such as gold. It is also the name of a loud music style: "Jeg lytter til metal" (I listen to metal).

sentence.da: Aluminium er et let **metal**.
sentence.en: Aluminum is a light metal.

et middagsselskab.explanation: "Et middagsselskab" means "a dinner party", an evening where people are invited to eat a meal together, often at home. "Selskab" means a gathering of guests and also a business: "et forsikringsselskab" (an insurance company).

sentence.da: Vi har inviteret venner til et **middagsselskab** på lørdag.
sentence.en: We have invited friends to a dinner party on Saturday.

et middel.explanation: "Et middel" means "a means", a way of reaching a goal, and also "a remedy", a product that helps against something: "et middel mod" (a remedy for). The plural "midler" also means "funds", as in "offentlige midler" (public funds).

sentence.da: Motion er et godt **middel** mod stress.
sentence.en: Exercise is a good remedy for stress.

et militær.explanation: "Et militær" means "a military", a country's armed forces. "Militær" also describes things: "et militært køretøj" (a military vehicle).

sentence.da: Landets **militær** har både soldater og skibe.
sentence.en: The country's military has both soldiers and ships.

et miljø.explanation: "Et miljø" means "an environment", the air, water and land around us, and also the surroundings people live or work in: "et godt arbejdsmiljø" (a good work environment).

sentence.da: Plastik i havet er dårligt for vores **miljø**.
sentence.en: Plastic in the sea is bad for our environment.

et mindretal.explanation: "Et mindretal" means "a minority", the smaller part of a group, fewer than half of the people or of the seats.

sentence.da: Kun et **mindretal** stemte for forslaget, så det faldt.
sentence.en: Only a minority voted for the proposal, so it failed.

et ministerium.explanation: "Et ministerium" means "a ministry", a part of the government headed by a minister. A ministry name is the subject it runs plus "ministeriet" (the ministry): "Finansministeriet" (the Ministry of Finance).

sentence.da: Skatteministeriet er et **ministerium**, der styrer skatten i landet.
sentence.en: The Ministry of Taxation is a ministry that manages taxes in the country.

et minut.explanation: "Et minut" means "a minute". To ask someone to wait, you can say "Vent et øjeblik" (wait a moment) or "Vent et minut" (wait a minute).

sentence.da: Et **minut** er tres sekunder.
sentence.en: A minute is sixty seconds.

et mirakel.explanation: "Et mirakel" means "a miracle", an event so unlikely that it seems impossible, and in religion an act of God that breaks the laws of nature.

sentence.da: Det er et **mirakel**, at han overlevede ulykken uden skader.
sentence.en: It is a miracle that he survived the accident without injuries.

et missil.explanation: "Et missil" means "a missile", a weapon that flies and explodes. A rocket for space or fireworks is "en raket" (a rocket).

sentence.da: Et **missil** ramte en bygning i nat.
sentence.en: A missile hit a building last night.

et modermærke.explanation: "Et modermærke" means "a mole", a small dark spot on the skin that you are born with or get over time. It is not the animal, which is "en muldvarp" (a mole).

sentence.da: Lægen kigger på det mørke **modermærke** på min ryg.
sentence.en: The doctor looks at the dark mole on my back.

et modersmål.explanation: "Et modersmål" means "a mother tongue", the speech you learned first as a child. "Mål" is an old word for speech.

sentence.da: Mit **modersmål** er engelsk, men jeg lærer dansk.
sentence.en: My mother tongue is English, but I am learning Danish.

et modeshow.explanation: "Et modeshow" means "a fashion show", an event where models walk and show new clothes. "Mode" (fashion) is joined to the English word "show".

sentence.da: Til et **modeshow** går modeller rundt i nyt tøj.
sentence.en: At a fashion show, models walk around in new clothes.

et modsætningsord.explanation: "Et modsætningsord" means "an antonym", a word that has the reverse meaning of another word.

sentence.da: Varm er et **modsætningsord** til kold.
sentence.en: Warm is an antonym of cold.

et molekyle.explanation: "Et molekyle" means "a molecule", a very small group of atoms joined together, such as water or sugar.

sentence.da: Hvert **molekyle** i vand har to brintatomer og ét iltatom.
sentence.en: Each molecule in water has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

et monster.explanation: "Et monster" means "a monster". Do not mix it up with "et mønster" (a pattern): "et mønster på tøjet" (a pattern on the cloth).

sentence.da: Barnet er bange for et **monster** under sengen.
sentence.en: The child is afraid of a monster under the bed.

et monument.explanation: "Et monument" means "a monument", a big structure that honors a person or an event. To name the person or event that a monument honors, use "for": "et monument for kongen" (a monument for the king).

sentence.da: Det store **monument** minder om krigen.
sentence.en: The big monument is a reminder of the war.

et mord.explanation: "Et mord" means "a murder", when one person kills another on purpose. You say "at begå mord" (to commit murder).

sentence.da: Politiet undersøger det **mord**, der skete i går.
sentence.en: The police are investigating the murder that happened yesterday.

et motel.explanation: "Et motel" means "a motel", a simple hotel by the road for people traveling by car.

sentence.da: Vi sover på et **motel** ved motorvejen.
sentence.en: We are sleeping at a motel by the highway.

et motiv.explanation: "Et motiv" means "a motive", the reason behind someone's action, and also "a subject", what a photo or a painting shows: "Motivet er en kirke" (The subject is a church).

sentence.da: Politiet leder stadig efter et **motiv** for forbrydelsen.
sentence.en: The police are still looking for a motive for the crime.

et museum.explanation: "Et museum" means "a museum", a place with art, history or science to look at. "På museet" means "at the museum".

sentence.da: Vi ser gamle ting på et **museum**.
sentence.en: We see old things at a museum.

et mysterium.explanation: "Et mysterium" means "a mystery", something strange or hidden that nobody can explain.

sentence.da: Hvordan pyramiderne blev bygget, er stadig et **mysterium**.
sentence.en: How the pyramids were built is still a mystery.

et mål.explanation: "Et mål" means "a goal", in life and in sports. "Han scorede to mål" (He scored two goals).

sentence.da: Mit **mål** er at tale godt dansk.
sentence.en: My goal is to speak good Danish.

et målebånd.explanation: "Et målebånd" means "a tape measure", a long, flexible strip with numbers that you use to measure length. It is built from at måle (to measure) and et bånd (a band).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger et **målebånd**, når jeg køber møbler.
sentence.en: I use a tape measure when I buy furniture.

et målebæger.explanation: "Et målebæger" means "a measuring cup", a cup with marks that show how much liquid or flour you pour. It is built from at måle (to measure) and et bæger (a cup).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger et **målebæger** til at måle sukker.
sentence.en: I use a measuring cup to measure sugar.

et måltid.explanation: "Et måltid" means "a meal", any occasion when you sit down to eat, like breakfast, lunch or dinner. It is the occasion, not the food itself, which is "mad" (food).

sentence.da: Dagens vigtigste **måltid** er morgenmad.
sentence.en: The most important meal of the day is breakfast.

et månedskort.explanation: "Et månedskort" means "a monthly pass", a ticket you can use as much as you like for a month. It is built from måned (month) and kort (card).

sentence.da: Med et **månedskort** kan jeg tage bussen hver dag.
sentence.en: With a monthly pass, I can take the bus every day.

et mærke.explanation: "Et mærke" means "a brand", and also "a mark" on a surface: "et mærke på væggen" (a mark on the wall).

sentence.da: Det er et dyrt **mærke**, men jakken er flot.
sentence.en: It is an expensive brand, but the jacket is nice.

et møbel.explanation: "Et møbel" means "a piece of furniture", such as a chair, a table or a bed. The plural "møbler" means "furniture": "Vi køber nye møbler" (We are buying new furniture).

sentence.da: En sofa er et **møbel**.
sentence.en: A sofa is a piece of furniture.

et møde.explanation: "Et møde" means "a meeting", for example at work.

sentence.da: Min chef har et **møde** i dag.
sentence.en: My boss has a meeting today.

et mødelokale.explanation: "Et mødelokale" means "a meeting room", a room at a workplace used for meetings. A "lokale" is a room in a public or work building, while "et værelse" (a room) is a room in a home or a hotel.

sentence.da: Kollegerne sidder i et **mødelokale** og planlægger det nye projekt.
sentence.en: The colleagues are sitting in a meeting room and planning the new project.

et mønster.explanation: "Et mønster" means "a pattern", a design that repeats, such as flowers or dots on cloth: "et mønster med blomster" (a pattern with flowers). It also means a pattern in what someone does: "et mønster i hans opførsel" (a pattern in his behavior).

sentence.da: Der er et fint **mønster** på kjolen.
sentence.en: There is a nice pattern on the dress.

mad.explanation: "Mad" means "food": "Jeg elsker dansk mad" (I love Danish food). For one dish, use "en ret" (a dish). Do not mix it up with "en mad", which means "a sandwich": "en mad med ost" (a sandwich with cheese).

sentence.da: Jeg er sulten og vil have **mad**.
sentence.en: I am hungry and want food.

madlavning.explanation: "Madlavning" means "cooking", the activity of making meals. To say someone is cooking right now, use "Han laver mad" (He is cooking).

sentence.da: Ved **madlavning** bruger vi en gryde og en pande.
sentence.en: When cooking, we use a pot and a pan.

madpapir.explanation: "Et madpapir" means "sandwich paper", the thin paper you wrap sandwiches in to take with you. It keeps the bread from drying out.

sentence.da: Jeg pakker madderne ind i **madpapir** og lægger dem i tasken.
sentence.en: I wrap the sandwiches in sandwich paper and put them in the bag.

madspild.explanation: "Et madspild" means "food waste", food that is bought or made but never eaten. It is built from mad (food) and spild (waste).

sentence.da: **Madspild** sker, når vi køber mere mad, end vi spiser.
sentence.en: Food waste happens when we buy more food than we eat.

mager.explanation: "Mager" means "lean" for food and "skinny" for people. For a person, it can sound negative, so "tynd" (thin) is milder.

sentence.da: En **mager** bøf har meget lidt fedt.
sentence.en: A lean steak has very little fat.

magi.explanation: "Magi" means "magic", the power to make impossible things happen, as in stories with spells. It also means a special, hard-to-explain charm: "Der er magi i luften" (There is magic in the air).

sentence.da: I eventyret bruger heksen **magi** til at forvandle prinsen til en frø.
sentence.en: In the fairy tale the witch uses magic to turn the prince into a frog.

magisk.explanation: "Magisk" means "magical", like magic in stories: "en magisk bog" (a magical book). It also describes a wonderful moment: "Det var magisk!" (It was magical!)

sentence.da: Troldmanden har en **magisk** stav i hånden.
sentence.en: The wizard has a magic wand in his hand.

magtfuld.explanation: "Magtfuld" means "powerful", for someone who has power over others, like rulers and big companies. For body strength, use "stærk" (strong).

sentence.da: Kongen var meget **magtfuld** og styrede hele landet.
sentence.en: The king was very powerful and ruled the whole country.

maj.explanation: "Maj" means "May" and sounds like the English word "my". Month names start with a lowercase letter in Danish, so you write "maj" in the middle of a sentence: "Det er varmt i maj" (It is warm in May).

sentence.da: **Maj** kommer efter april og før juni.
sentence.en: May comes after April and before June.

majs.explanation: "Majs" means "corn", the yellow kind you eat as a vegetable. It is used without "en": "Jeg spiser majs" (I eat corn).

sentence.da: Popcorn er lavet af **majs**.
sentence.en: Popcorn is made of corn.

makeup.explanation: "Makeup" means "makeup", the same word as in English. To put it on, say "tage makeup på": "Hun tager makeup på" (She puts on makeup).

sentence.da: Hun bruger **makeup** på øjne og læber.
sentence.en: She uses makeup on her eyes and lips.

maksimal.explanation: "Maksimal" means "maximum", the biggest amount that is allowed or possible.

sentence.da: Bilen kører med **maksimal** hastighed på motorvejen.
sentence.en: The car drives at maximum speed on the highway.

malerisk.explanation: "Malerisk" means "picturesque", so lovely to look at that it seems made for a picture: "en malerisk landsby" (a picturesque village).

sentence.da: Den lille by med gamle huse og smalle gader er **malerisk**.
sentence.en: The small town with old houses and narrow streets is picturesque.

maling.explanation: "Maling" means "paint". A picture on a wall is "et maleri" (a painting), not maling.

sentence.da: Vi skal bruge blå **maling** til soveværelset.
sentence.en: We need blue paint for the bedroom.

man.explanation: "Man" means "you" or "one", for anybody. "Du kan købe billetter" (You can buy tickets) talks to one person, while "Man kan købe billetter her" (You can buy tickets here) is true for anyone. Do not mix it up with "en mand" (a man): "Der står en mand her" (A man is standing here).

sentence.da: Her må **man** ikke parkere.
sentence.en: You may not park here.

man skal ikke skue hunden på hårene.explanation: "Man skal ikke skue hunden på hårene" means "don't judge a book by its cover". Literally it says you should not judge the dog by its hair. "Skue" is an old word meaning "look at", and the saying is used when someone turns out different from how they looked.

forms.da: Man skal ikke skue hunden på hårene!
forms.en: Don't judge a book by its cover!

forms.da: Jeg troede, han var sur, men man skal ikke skue hunden på hårene
forms.en: I thought he was grumpy, but don't judge a book by its cover

related.da: det er ikke guld alt, hvad der glimrer
related.en: all that glitters is not gold

sentence.da: Hun ser streng ud, men **man skal ikke skue hunden på hårene**.
sentence.en: She looks strict, but don't judge a book by its cover.

mandag.explanation: "En mandag" means "a Monday". "På mandag" means "on Monday" (the coming one), "om mandagen" means "on Mondays" (every Monday), and "i mandags" means "last Monday". Day names start with a lowercase letter in Danish.

sentence.da: Ugen begynder med **mandag**.
sentence.en: The week begins with Monday.

mandlig.explanation: "Mandlig" means "male" and is built on mand (man). It is used for people and animals: "en mandlig kollega" (a male colleague), "en mandlig løve" (a male lion).

sentence.da: Han er en **mandlig** sygeplejerske.
sentence.en: He is a male nurse.

manerer.explanation: "Manerer" means "manners", the way a person behaves around others.

sentence.da: Børn lærer **manerer**, når de spiser sammen med de voksne.
sentence.en: Children learn manners when they eat together with the adults.

mange.explanation: "Mange" means "many", for things you can count: "mange biler" (many cars). For things you pour or measure, such as water, use "meget" (a lot, much): "meget vand" (a lot of water).

sentence.da: Jeg har **mange** venner.
sentence.en: I have many friends.

mange tak.explanation: "Mange tak" means "many thanks" and is stronger than "tak" (thanks). To name the reason for your thanks, add "for" (for): "Mange tak for hjælpen" (Thank you very much for the help). People reply "selv tak" (you're welcome) or "ingen årsag" (no problem).

forms.en: Thank you very much for the help.

sentence.da: Her er din kaffe. – **Mange tak**!
sentence.en: Here is your coffee. – Thank you very much!

mangelfuld.explanation: "Mangelfuld" means "inadequate" or "deficient", for something that is not good enough, such as information, work or equipment: "mangelfuld information" (inadequate information). It is built from mangel (shortage) and -fuld (full of), so it is literally "full of shortage".

sentence.da: Forklaringen var **mangelfuld**, og vi forstod den ikke.
sentence.en: The explanation was inadequate and we did not understand it.

mangfoldighed.explanation: "Mangfoldighed" means "diversity", many different kinds in one place: "kulturel mangfoldighed" (cultural diversity).

sentence.da: Naturen byder på en stor **mangfoldighed** af planter og dyr.
sentence.en: Nature offers a great diversity of plants and animals.

manglende.explanation: "Manglende" means "missing", for something that is not there but should be: "en manglende side" (a missing page).

sentence.da: Den **manglende** brik til puslespillet lå under sofaen.
sentence.en: The missing piece of the puzzle was under the sofa.

marcipan.explanation: "Marcipan" means "marzipan", a sweet paste of almonds and sugar. It is used to cover cakes and to make sweets.

sentence.da: Kagen er fyldt med **marcipan** og mandler.
sentence.en: The cake is filled with marzipan and almonds.

marihuana.explanation: "Marihuana" means "marijuana", the dried parts of the hemp plant that people use to get high. Danish spells it with an h where English has a j.

sentence.da: Det er ulovligt at sælge **marihuana** i Danmark.
sentence.en: It is illegal to sell marijuana in Denmark.

markant.explanation: "Markant" means "marked" or "distinctive", clearly noticeable because it stands out. For a change or a difference: "en markant forbedring" (a marked improvement). For a person with a strong presence: "en markant politiker" (a prominent politician).

sentence.da: Der er en **markant** forskel mellem sommer og vinter her.
sentence.en: There is a marked difference between summer and winter here.

marmelade.explanation: "Marmelade" means "jam" or "marmalade", a sweet fruit spread for bread. Another everyday word for it is "syltetøj" (jam).

sentence.da: Hun spiser brød med smør og **marmelade**.
sentence.en: She eats bread with butter and jam.

marmor.explanation: "Et marmor" means "marble", a hard, smooth rock used in floors, kitchen counters and statues.

sentence.da: Statuen er hugget i **marmor**, ikke i træ.
sentence.en: The statue is carved in marble, not in wood.

marts.explanation: "Marts" means "March". Month names start with a lowercase letter in Danish. Dates are said like "den tiende marts" (the tenth of March).

sentence.da: Efter februar kommer **marts**.
sentence.en: After February comes March.

masser af.explanation: "Masser af" means "lots of": "masser af mad" (lots of food), "masser af venner" (lots of friends).

sentence.da: Vi har **masser af** tid i dag.
sentence.en: We have lots of time today.

sentence.da: I **matematik** lærer vi at regne med tal.
sentence.en: In math we learn to calculate with numbers.

materiel.explanation: "Materiel" means "material", about things you can touch or own, as opposed to ideas and feelings: "materielle goder" (material goods). Do not mix it up with "et materiale" (a material), which is a substance such as wood or cloth.

sentence.da: Branden gav kun **materiel** skade, og ingen blev såret.
sentence.en: The fire caused only material damage, and nobody was hurt.

mayonnaise.explanation: "Mayonnaise" means "mayonnaise", the thick white sauce. In everyday talk, you can shorten it to "mayo" (mayo).

sentence.da: Man laver **mayonnaise** af æg og olie.
sentence.en: You make mayonnaise from egg and oil.

med.explanation: "Med" means "with". Its opposite is "uden" (without): "kaffe uden mælk" (coffee without milk). It is also used for coming or going along: "tage med" (to take along), "gå med" (to go along).

forms.en: a cup of coffee with milk

sentence.da: Jeg drikker kaffe **med** mælk.
sentence.en: I drink coffee with milk.

med andre ord.explanation: "Med andre ord" means "in other words" and says the same thing again or sums it up: "Bilen er gået i stykker. Med andre ord må vi tage toget" (The car broke down. In other words, we must take the train).

sentence.da: Han er syg. **Med andre ord** kommer han ikke.
sentence.en: He is sick. In other words, he is not coming.

med det samme.explanation: "Med det samme" means "right away" or "immediately". For something soon but not this second, use "om lidt" (in a little while): "Jeg kommer om lidt" (I am coming in a little while).

sentence.da: Jeg kommer **med det samme**.
sentence.en: I'm coming right away.

med forsæt.explanation: "Med forsæt" means "on purpose" for a harmful act that was meant, as in courts and the news: "Branden blev startet med forsæt" (The fire was started on purpose). In everyday talk, say "med vilje" (on purpose): "Jeg gjorde det med vilje" (I did it on purpose).

sentence.da: Retten mener, at han ødelagde bilen **med forsæt**.
sentence.en: The court believes he destroyed the car on purpose.

med hensyn til.explanation: "Med hensyn til" means "regarding". Say it to name the topic you are about to talk about: "Med hensyn til prisen har jeg et spørgsmål" (Regarding the price, I have a question).

sentence.da: **Med hensyn til** mødet i morgen kan jeg desværre ikke komme.
sentence.en: Regarding the meeting tomorrow, I unfortunately cannot come.

medfølelse.explanation: "En medfølelse" means "compassion", the feeling of sharing someone's pain and wanting to help. It is built from med (with) and følelse (feeling), so it is feeling with someone, not looking down on them.

sentence.da: Hun viste **medfølelse** og holdt ham i hånden, da han græd.
sentence.en: She showed compassion and held his hand when he cried.

medicin.explanation: "En medicin" means "a medicine", something you take when you are ill.

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og tager **medicin**.
sentence.en: I am sick and take medicine.

medicinsk.explanation: "Medicinsk" means "medical", for things to do with illness and treatment: "medicinsk behandling" (medical treatment), "et medicinsk problem" (a medical problem).

sentence.da: Lægen mener, at smerten har en **medicinsk** årsag.
sentence.en: The doctor thinks the pain has a medical cause.

medlidenhed.explanation: "En medlidenhed" means "pity", the sad feeling for someone who suffers. It can feel like looking down on a person, so some do not want it: "Jeg vil ikke have din medlidenhed" (I do not want your pity).

sentence.da: Han følte **medlidenhed** med hunden, som stod alene i regnen.
sentence.en: He felt pity for the dog that stood alone in the rain.

medmindre.explanation: "Medmindre" means "unless". It introduces the one case in which what you just said will not happen: "Jeg kommer, medmindre jeg bliver syg" (I will come unless I get sick).

sentence.da: Vi tager til stranden, **medmindre** det regner.
sentence.en: We are going to the beach unless it rains.

megen.explanation: "Megen" means "much" and goes before an en-word such as "tid" (time): "megen tid" (much time). Before an et-word use "meget" (much): "meget vand" (much water). You mostly see it in sentences with "ikke" (not) or with "for" (too): "for megen støj" (too much noise).

sentence.da: Jeg har ikke **megen** tid.
sentence.en: I do not have much time.

meget.explanation: "Meget" means "very" before a describing word: "meget god" (very good). Before a thing you cannot count one by one, such as water, it means "a lot" or "much": "meget vand" (a lot of water). Before things you count one by one, use "mange" (many): "mange biler" (many cars).

forms.en: I have a lot of time.

sentence.da: Det er **meget** koldt i dag.
sentence.en: It is very cold today.

mel.explanation: "Mel" means "flour", the white powder you bake with: "Jeg bager med mel" (I bake with flour).

sentence.da: Jeg bager brød med **mel**.
sentence.en: I bake bread with flour.

mellem.explanation: "Mellem" means "between", for places, times and amounts: "mellem to og tre" (between two and three). It also works for a difference: "forskellen mellem dem" (the difference between them).

forms.en: between the house and the forest

sentence.da: Banken ligger **mellem** posthuset og skolen.
sentence.en: The bank is between the post office and the school.

mellemøsten.explanation: "Mellemøsten" means "the Middle East". It is a place name, so it starts with an uppercase letter. It is built from mellem (between) and øst (east).

forms.en: to travel to the Middle East
the war in the Middle East

sentence.da: Det er varmt og tørt i **Mellemøsten**.
sentence.en: It is hot and dry in the Middle East.

men.explanation: "Men" means "but". It joins two ideas that go against each other: "Jeg er træt, men jeg kommer" (I am tired, but I am coming). Do not mix it up with "mens" (while).

sentence.da: Jeg er træt, **men** glad.
sentence.en: I am tired, but happy.

meningsfuld.explanation: "Meningsfuld" means "meaningful", for something that has a point or feels worth your time.

sentence.da: Samtalen var **meningsfuld**, fordi vi endelig forstod hinanden.
sentence.en: The conversation was meaningful because we finally understood each other.

meningsløs.explanation: "Meningsløs" means "meaningless", with no point or sense. The ending -løs means "without", as in "hjælpeløs" (helpless).

sentence.da: Diskussionen var **meningsløs**, fordi ingen ville lytte.
sentence.en: The discussion was pointless because nobody wanted to listen.

menneskehed.explanation: "Menneskehed" means "humanity", people everywhere: "Det er godt for hele menneskeheden" (It is good for all of humanity). The quality of being kind and humane is a different word: "menneskelighed" (humaneness).

sentence.da: Mange drømmer om en **menneskehed** uden krig.
sentence.en: Many dream of a humanity without war.

menneskelig.explanation: "Menneskelig" means "human": "en menneskelig fejl" (a human mistake). It can also mean kind and understanding: "en menneskelig chef" (a kind boss).

sentence.da: Det er en **menneskelig** fejl, ikke en computerfejl.
sentence.en: It is a human mistake, not a computer error.

menneskerettigheder.explanation: "Menneskerettigheder" means "human rights", the basic rights that every person has, whoever they are and wherever they live, such as the right to live and speak freely.

sentence.da: **Menneskerettigheder** gælder for alle, uanset hvor man bor.
sentence.en: Human rights apply to everyone, no matter where one lives.

mens.explanation: "Mens" means "while". It joins two things that happen at the same time: "Hun synger, mens hun laver mad" (She sings while she cooks). Do not mix it up with "men" (but).

sentence.da: Jeg læser, **mens** du sover.
sentence.en: I read while you sleep.

mental sundhed.explanation: "Mental sundhed" means "mental health", how well your mind and feelings are doing, not only whether you are ill.

sentence.da: God **mental sundhed** handler om søvn, venner og ro i hverdagen.
sentence.en: Good mental health is about sleep, friends and calm in everyday life.

mentalt.explanation: "Mentalt" means "mentally", in the mind rather than the body.

sentence.da: Før løbet forbereder løberne sig både fysisk og **mentalt**.
sentence.en: Before the race the runners prepare both physically and mentally.

mere.explanation: "Mere" means "more" before a thing you cannot count one by one, such as water: "mere vand" (more water). Before a describing word it makes a comparison: "mere interessant" (more interesting). With "ikke" (not), it means "any longer": "Jeg bor ikke her mere" (I don't live here anymore). Before things you count one by one, use "flere" (more): "flere biler" (more cars).

sentence.da: Jeg er sulten og vil have **mere** mad.
sentence.en: I am hungry and want more food.

mest.explanation: "Mest" means "most" or "mostly": "Jeg læser mest krimier" (I mostly read crime novels). Before a describing word it means "the most": "mest interessant" (most interesting).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **mest** lide kaffe.
sentence.en: I like coffee the most.

mexicansk.explanation: "Mexicansk" means "Mexican" and describes things from Mexico. A person from Mexico is "en mexicaner" (a Mexican).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **mexicansk** mad hver fredag.
sentence.en: We eat Mexican food every Friday.

middelalderen.explanation: "Middelalderen" means "the Middle Ages", the long stretch of European history before the modern age. In longer words, "middelalder-" means "medieval": "en middelalderby" (a medieval town).

sentence.da: I **middelalderen** boede de fleste danskere på landet og dyrkede jorden.
sentence.en: In the Middle Ages most Danes lived in the countryside and farmed the land.

midlertidig.explanation: "Midlertidig" means "temporary", in place only for a short while and meant to be replaced later: "en midlertidig løsning" (a temporary solution).

sentence.da: Broen er **midlertidig**, fordi den nye bro ikke er færdig.
sentence.en: The bridge is temporary because the new bridge is not finished.
